title: Ibn Abbas
hookLine: the young cousin, prayed for to understand the religion, later the great interpreter (Bukhari)

lines: A JUG OF WATER, SET OUT.
A ONE-LINE PRAYER FOR A BOY.
cards: A jug of water has been set out. Nobody asked for it. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, comes to wash, finds it waiting, and asks: who put this here?
Someone tells him: Abdullah, the son of your uncle Abbas. A boy, who had noticed what would be needed and quietly set it out.
And instead of a thank you, the Prophet says a short prayer for him, one line the boy will carry for the rest of his life. Today: Ibn Abbas.

teach.b: Sahih al-Bukhari records the prayer: O God, give him understanding of the religion. In Arabic, the prayer asks that he be given fiqh in the religion, the word later used for the study of Islamic law.

teach.h: O GOD, TEACH HIM THE BOOK.
teach.b: In another report in Bukhari, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet held him close and prayed: O God, teach him the book. Did it show? Bukhari keeps a scene that answers.

Years later, Umar, now leading the community, used to bring young Ibn Abbas into his council with the older men who had fought at Badr. Some of them objected: why does he sit with us, when we have sons his age?

So one day Umar asked the whole group about the surah that begins: when the help of God comes, and the victory. Some said it tells us to praise God and seek His forgiveness when victory comes. Others said nothing.
Then Umar turned to Ibn Abbas. Is that what you say too? No, he said.

It was the sign of the Prophet's own approaching death, given to him by God: when the victory comes, your work is done; praise your Lord and ask forgiveness. Umar answered: I know nothing of it except what you have said.
The older men gave the plain meaning, and it was true.
The young man saw what the surah was pointing to. Tradition remembers Ibn Abbas as an interpreter of the Qur'an. It started with a jug of water and a one-line prayer.

how: Muslims remember Abdullah ibn Abbas as a companion known for explaining the Qur'an, and retell the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari where the Prophet prayed for him to be given understanding of the religion.

games.q: you are the Prophet. you step out to wash for prayer and find water already set out for you. a boy put it there. what do you do?
o: thank him and send him home.
pray for him: O God, give him understanding of the religion.
tell him to ask first next time.
games.why: Bukhari records the one-line prayer for understanding. tradition remembers the boy as an interpreter of the Qur'an.

practice: Take the first line of surah one hundred ten, when the help of God comes, and the victory, and say it once, slowly.
Then ask Ibn Abbas's kind of question, not only what it says but what it is doing, who it speaks to, what moment it is for, and sit with it without hurrying.
If you pray, you can ask, as the Prophet asked for him, for understanding.

wordCard.voice: Ibn Abbas. Abdullah, son of the Prophet's uncle Abbas, prayed for as a boy to understand the religion and the book, and remembered as an interpreter of the Qur'an. Today's word, and the last of the early believers.

orig.note: Arabic: 'understanding'; the word in the prayer 'give him understanding of the religion', and later the name for Islamic law.

carryVoice: Your line: understanding prayed for. Tomorrow the path turns to the later companions and their stories. See you there.
